question: An insulin pen that is currently in use (being used daily) should be stored in the refrigerator between injections to maintain potency.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. In-use insulin pens are stored at room temperature (<25-30°C) for up to 4 weeks — not in the refrigerator. Injecting cold insulin is painful and can affect absorption. Only spare (unopened) insulin should be refrigerated at 2-8°C.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Insulin pens in current use should be stored at room temperature (below 25-30°C) away from light and heat for up to 4 weeks. Refrigerated insulin injected cold is painful and may impair absorption. Spare/unopened insulin should be refrigerated (2-8°C).
